claims.text: Elevated-temperature stress–strain behavior in HfNbTaTiZr is influenced by temperature-dependent elastic anisotropic deformation.
Elevated-temperature thermal expansion in HfNbTaTiZr is influenced by temperature-dependent elastic anisotropic deformation.
Elevated-temperature elastic behavior in HfNbTaTiZr is influenced by temperature-dependent elastic anisotropic deformation.
Plastic deformation of HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperature is dominated by edge dislocations.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr material is polycrystalline.
High-temperature neutron diffraction can be used to characterize the proposed deformation behavior under loading.
Edge dislocations constitute a structural mediator of the elevated-temperature mechanical response.
Elastic anisotropic deformation constitutes a structural mediator of the elevated-temperature response.
The proposed behavior may improve yield strength at elevated temperatures.
The proposed behavior may improve resistance to elevated-temperature softening.
Room-temperature or low-temperature HfNbTaTiZr behavior is the proposed baseline.
The proposed hypothesis is intended to apply from 500 to 1000 °C.
The proposed hypothesis is intended to apply over a strain range of 0–10%.
The effects of composition and microstructure on elevated-temperature mechanical properties are not fully understood.
